A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same anTransformer/anGPT research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated material can be matched, including v1 Appendix E to v2 Appendix P and v1 Appendix I to v2 Appendix J.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, runtime measurements, scaling fits, architectural ablations and optimization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds downstream benchmark results, normalization-factor ablations and robustness measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture and Table 1 remain unchanged. However, new Appendix E gives an output-projection factor of 1 and a reciprocal-square-root residual factor, conflicting with the formulas retained in Section 4.3. The PDFs do not establish whether the implemented normalization changed or conflicting documentation was added.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds evaluation on PIQA, ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, WikiText, WinoGrande and MMLU. Appendix O adds a pathological repeated-token input scenario. These substantially expand evaluation beyond the retained SlimPajama and OpenWebText language-modeling experiments.

E2.justification: Matching comparisons retain GPT+, nGPT, GPT+ without QK normalization, LN scaling and DyT. The added downstream and stability comparisons use the existing GPT+ comparator; no competing method is added or removed from the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds accuracy/perplexity evaluation of 1B models at 10B, 21B and 42B training tokens, factor-rescaling/removal controls, and testing with 512 repetitions of one token. Table F.2 also changes anGPT's initialization from 0.01 to 0.001, although Section 5 still states 0.01; this reported setting conflict does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained architectural ablation, v2 adds normalization-factor and LERP ablations, interpolation-parameter trajectories, norm-propagation and approximation-error measurements, and distribution-shift testing in Appendices L–O. Appendix I adds explicit convergence-speedup analysis across model scales. The old parameter-norm plot merely moves from Appendix E to P.

E5.justification: The scaling-exponent Z-test and its p=0.073 result disappear from v2 Appendix J, while the confidence-interval calculation and bands remain. New Table O.1 reports residual-norm standard deviations without specifying their sampling basis. Both versions still acknowledge that training was not repeated across random seeds.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical findings in Appendices K–O. For example, at 42B tokens, ARC-Easy accuracy is 0.596 for anGPT versus 0.561 for GPT+; MMLU at 10B is tied at 0.232. Table L.1 reports loss 7.935 when all normalization factors are halved and NaN when doubled. The existing main pretraining results, runtime values and scaling-fit parameters remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the missing zero-mean assumption for independent residual contributions and explicitly expands the cross terms before deriving expected squared norm L. This repairs a gap in the earlier derivation. The concentration theorem and principal normalization derivations remain.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain approximate normalization, bounded parameters, removal of weight decay and warm-up, roughly 40% faster convergence with about 3% runtime overhead, and favorable scaling. Abstract and conclusion revisions largely restate claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting downstream gains to pretraining loss, interpolation parameters to feature incorporation, and residual normalization to stability and failure. It expands discussion of violated normalization assumptions and possible FP8 applications. However, Section 6 retains the now-contradictory statement that downstream tasks were not evaluated.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly provides an anGPT implementation link. Appendix E consolidates normalization formulas and specifies 100,000 Monte Carlo samples for the activation factor, while Section 4.3 elaborates the existing parameter reparameterization. Most hardware, data-processing and training details are retained, although the new formula and initialization inconsistencies limit reproducibility.

R1.justification: The same 38 cited works and substantive positioning against nGPT, depth-dependent normalization scaling, DyT and constrained parameter regularization remain. Added bibliographic URLs do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and optimization explanation, edits prose throughout, separates Discussion from Conclusion, and integrates new evaluation subsections and appendices. The main organizational sequence and much of the existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds convergence and interpolation-trajectory figures plus downstream, ablation, norm-ratio, estimation-error and distribution-shift tables. It also reformats Figure 4, merges the nGPT/anGPT columns in Table F.2, and relocates existing appendix displays. These substantially expand the visual presentation beyond simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: The downstream evaluations and targeted ablations provide useful evidence beyond v1's pretraining-loss comparisons, while Section 3.2 repairs a mathematical assumption and Appendix F adds implementation access information. These gains are limited by conflicting normalization formulas and initialization values, sparse downstream evaluation details, and the stale no-downstream-evaluation limitation. The empirical support improves, but the reporting inconsistencies prevent a stronger overall improvement judgment.
